source_text: V. Martianus ait: Quod discere semper optabam, repente confessus es errorem vestrae persuasionis et legis. habet ergo, ut dicis, filium deus? respondit Achatius: Habet. Martianus ait: Quis est filius dei? respondit Achatius: Verbum veritatis et gratiae. Martianus ait: Hoc habet nomen? respondit Achatius: Non de nomine interrogaveras, sed de ipsa filii potestate. Martianus ait: Nomen explana. sanctus Achatius respondit: Iesus Christus vocatur. Martianus ait: Ex qua dei uxore conceptus est? respondit sanctus Achatius: Non hominum more deus filium ex muliebri coitu genuit, sed Adam primum dextera sua faciente formavit. nam absit ut tu maiestati divinae contactum puellae mortalis affirmes. luto primi hominis membra composuit, et ubi integram iam compleverat effigiem, animam spiritumque concessit. sic et filius dei verbum veritatis ex dei corde processit. ideo scriptum est: Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum. Martianus ait: Corporalis igitur deus est? Achatius dixit: Ipse solus agnoscit, nos vero non cognoscimus invisibilem formam, sed virtutem potentiamque veneramur. Martianus ait: Si in corpore non est, etiam cordis ignarus est. nam sensus non potest esse sine membris. respondit Achatius: Non in his membris sapientia nascitur, sed a deo datur. quid ergo pertinet corpus ad sensum? Martianus ait: Cataphryges aspice, homines religionis antiquae, ad mea sacra conversos reliquisse quae fuerant, et nobiscum diis vota persolvere: et tu similiter parere festina. omnes catholicae legis collige Christianos et cum his religionem nostri imperatoris attende. veniat tecum omnis populus, ex tuo pendet arbitrio: respondit Achatius: Illi omnes non meo nutu, sed dei praecepto reguntur. audiant me itaque, si iusta persuadeam; sin vero perversa et nocitura, contemnant.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus says Achatius has suddenly admitted what he always wanted to learn, the error of their persuasion and law, and asks if God then has a Son; Achatius says He has, that the Son of God is the Word of truth and grace, and when pressed for the Name answers Jesus Christ, explaining that God did not beget by human intercourse but formed the first Adam by His right hand from clay and gave soul and spirit, and so the Son proceeded as Word from God's heart, as written; to whether God is therefore bodily Achatius says only God knows, we do not know the invisible form but venerate virtue and power; to the objection that without body there is no heart or sense without limbs he replies wisdom is not born in limbs but given by God; Martianus then points to the Cataphrygians turned to his rites and urges obedience and gathering the Christians to the emperor's religion, with the people depending on him; Achatius replies they are ruled not by his nod but by God's command, to be heard if he persuades just things and rejected if perverse and harmful.
pass_b_english: Martianus said, What I always desired to learn you have suddenly confessed, the error of your persuasion and law.
Has God, then, as you say, a Son?
Achatius answered, He has.
Martianus said, Who is the Son of God?
Achatius answered, The Word of truth and grace.
Martianus said, Is this his name?
Achatius answered, You had asked not about the name but about the very power of the Son.
Martianus said, Declare the name.
Holy Achatius answered, He is called Jesus Christ.
Martianus said, From which wife of God was he conceived?
Holy Achatius answered, God did not beget the Son after the manner of men from union with a woman, but with His own right hand fashioning He formed the first Adam.
For far be it that you should ascribe to the divine majesty contact with a mortal maiden.
From clay He put together the limbs of the first man, and when He had already completed the whole figure He granted soul and spirit.
So also the Son of God, the Word of truth, came forth from the heart of God, for it is written, My heart has uttered a good word (Psalms 44:2 LXX).
Martianus said, Is God therefore bodily?
Achatius said, He alone knows; we do not know the invisible form, but we venerate His virtue and power.
Martianus said, If He is not in a body, He is also without knowledge of the heart.
For sense cannot exist without limbs.
Achatius answered, Wisdom is not born in these limbs, but is given by God.
What then has the body to do with sense?
Martianus said, Look at the Cataphrygians, men of the ancient religion, turned to my rites, having left what they had been, and with us paying vows to the gods; so you likewise hasten to obey.
Gather all the Christians of the catholic law and with them observe the religion of our emperor.
Let every people come with you; it hangs upon your decision.
Achatius answered, They are all ruled not by my nod but by the command of God.
Let them therefore hear me if I persuade just things; but if perverse and harmful things, let them reject me.

lemmas.gloss: party opinion or sect belief here
rank or power of the Son here
came forth from God's heart here
uttered forth in the psalm verse here
nod or will of a man here

choices.why: genitives veritatis et gratiae define what the Word is and gives, not a proper name, as the next exchange contrasts name with potestas

choices.english: by His right hand making him
choices.why: ablative absolute with present participle keeps God's hand as instrumental agent of forming Adam, against a mortal begetting reading
paired abstract nouns contrasted with invisibilem formam, so moral efficacy and might rather than an army or miracle
